candidates.description: This vector is activated by common Chinese characters and subwords in multilingual tokenizers.
This feature vector is sensitive to indefinite articles and similar determiners across different languages.
These tokens represent common German adverbial modifiers of degree, time, and emphasis.
The feature vector activates on the phonetic sequence "sh" and words containing it.
This vector activates strongly on tokens starting with the German indefinite article "ein" or its common morphological variations and similarly spelled roots.
This vector activates on the German letter "ü" (U-umlaut) both as an independent character and as a common prefix or root component in German words.
These tokens are German third-person or plural present-tense verb forms commonly used in formal or instructional contexts.
These tokens represent German modal verbs and auxiliary verbs expressing necessity, ability, or permission.
This vector represents common German verb forms, including various tenses and conjugations.
This feature vector represents German negation words, prefixes, and common grammatical components.
